text: Why can a truth table define a logical operator completely?
choices: There are finitely many input combinations, so all of them can be listed
Because two-valued logic has no edge cases
Because the operators are all commutative
Because logic is simpler than arithmetic
explanation: Two boolean inputs give four rows, and listing all four leaves nothing to interpretation and no case forgotten. This kind of verification by exhaustion is possible here and impossible for programs generally, which is why Chapter 9 needs invariants.
